1	---
2	type: Playbook
3	title: Line Build — Kitchen Prep Line Assignments
4	description: How Cookbook line builds define cooking lines, appliances, phases, tasks, steps, and hot-hold workflows for truck items, plus the nested-JSON query patterns to extract them from BigQuery.
5	tags: [cookbook, bigquery, line-build, kitchen-ops]
6	timestamp: 2026-06-22
7	access: open
8	---
9	
10	# Line Build - Kitchen Prep Line Assignments
11	
12	The line build system defines how items are prepared in the kitchen, including which cooking line, appliance, and phase each step belongs to. This is critical for kitchen operations and KDS (Kitchen Display System) sequencing.
13	
14	Line builds are **only applicable to truck items** (items prepared on Wonder trucks/HDRs). They define the complete cooking workflow from prep through completion.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Essential Filter (ALWAYS USE)
19	
20	When joining to item tables, always include:
21	
22	```sql
23	WHERE effective = true
24	  AND deleted = false
25	  AND item_status != 'DORMANT'
26	```
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Line Build Status
31	
32	Each line build has a status indicating its readiness:
33	
34	| Status | Description |
35	|--------|-------------|
36	| `None` | No line build exists for this truck item version |
37	| `Line Build Created` | Line build exists and is valid |
38	| `Pending Update` | Line build exists but has warnings requiring attention |
39	
40	When warnings exist (e.g., BOM changes affecting line build), status changes to `Pending Update`.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## Line Build Hierarchy
45	
46	Line builds follow a hierarchical structure:
47	
48	```
49	Line Build (per item version)
50	├── Apply to Restaurants (All or specific HDRs)
51	├── Apply to Options (customization variants)
52	└── Tasks (parallel cooking workflows)
53	    └── Steps (ordered actions within task)
54	        └── Sub-Steps (detailed instructions per step)
55	```
56	
57	### Multi-Task Line Builds
58	
59	A menu item can have **multiple parallel tasks** within a single line build. Tasks enable:
60	- Component-based cooking (different proteins cooked separately)
61	- Customization-driven workflows (sauce trio only if selected)
62	- Parallel prep paths that converge at expo
63	
64	**Task Properties:**
65	- `task_name` - Required, up to 100 characters (e.g., "Flatbread", "Chicken Kebab", "Sauce Trio")
66	- `mapping_option` - Optional customization option that triggers this task
67	
68	**Important:** No step dependencies across parallel tasks. Dependencies exist only within individual tasks.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## Activity Types
73	
74	The `procedures_activity` field indicates what type of action is performed:
75	
76	| Activity | Description | Use Case | Required Fields |
77	|----------|-------------|----------|-----------------|
78	| `COOK` | Active cooking action | Frying, grilling, baking | Appliance required, cook time > 0 |
79	| `GARNISH` | Assembly/garnishing | Adding toppings, plating | Step time > 0, no appliance |
80	| `COMPLETE` | Completion/finishing | Final packaging, handoff | Must be last step, parking spot required |
81	| `VEND` | Vending/dispensing | Packaged items from ambient storage | Mapping item required, parking spot required |
82	
83	> **Deprecated**: The `PACKAGE` and `BAG` activities are deprecated. They may appear in historical data but should not be used in new line builds.
84	
85	**Activity-Specific Rules:**
86	
87	- **COOK**: Must have appliance selected; step time > cook time
88	- **GARNISH**: No appliance; cook time and resting time = 0
89	- **COMPLETE**: Must be last step; exactly one complete step per task (unless customization variants)
90	- **VEND**: Only shows BOM items (excluding hot hold eligible items) and customization options; requires parking spot (Ambient or Warm)
91	
92	---
93	
94	## Core Table
95	
96	### item_line_builds
97	
98	Kitchen prep line assignments with timing and equipment details. See [../tables/secure-recipe-prod/recipe_v2/item_line_builds.md](../tables/secure-recipe-prod/recipe_v2/item_line_builds.md).
99	
100	```sql
101	-- Key identification fields
102	item_version_id          STRING    -- Version UUID
103	item_number              STRING    -- Item ID
104	service_start_time       DATETIME  -- Service window start
105	service_end_time         DATETIME  -- Service window end
106	line_build_id            STRING    -- Unique line build identifier
107	status                   STRING    -- Line build status
108	restaurant_id            STRING    -- Associated HDR/restaurant
109	
110	-- Procedure fields
111	procedures_step_order    INTEGER   -- Order of this step
112	procedures_cooking_phase STRING    -- Cooking phase (see below)
113	procedures_appliance     STRING    -- Equipment used (see below)
114	procedures_activity      STRING    -- Activity description
115	procedures_batch_limit   STRING    -- Batch limit
116	procedures_holding_location STRING -- Where item is held
117	
118	-- Timing fields
119	step_time                STRING    -- Total step time
120	cooking_time             STRING    -- Active cooking time
121	resting_time             STRING    -- Resting/cooling time
122	hold_time                STRING    -- Hold time before service
123	
124	-- Hot hold eligibility
125	is_hot_hold_eligible_selected BOOLEAN -- Can be held hot
126	show_hot_hold            BOOLEAN   -- Display hot hold option
127	
128	-- Sub-steps (nested detail)
129	sub_steps_order          STRING    -- Sub-step ordering
130	sub_steps_title          STRING    -- Sub-step title
131	sub_steps_related_item_number STRING -- Related item if any
132	```
133	
134	## Cooking Phases
135	
136	| Phase | Description |
137	|-------|-------------|
138	| `PRE_ROUTE_PREP` | Preparation before routing/assignment |
139	| `PRE_ORDER_PREP` | Preparation before order received |
140	| `PRE_COOKING` | Prep work before cooking starts |
141	| `COOKING` | Active cooking phase |
142	| `POST_COOKING` | Assembly/finishing after cooking |
143	
144	> **Note**: The `HOT_HOLD` and `A_LA_MINUTE` values do not exist in the current cooking phase enum. Hot hold functionality is managed through the hot hold eligible flags and appliance configurations, not as a cooking phase.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## Appliances
149	
150	Appliances available by activity type:
151	
152	### COOK Activity Appliances
153	
154	| Appliance | Use Case | Global Config Required |
155	|-----------|----------|------------------------|
156	| `TURBO_OVEN` | Rapid convection heating | Yes - `{percent}/{windspeed} {temp}` (e.g., "100/90 475°F") |
157	| `FRYER` | Deep frying | Yes - temperature (325°F, 350°F) |
158	| `PIZZA_CONVEYOR_OVEN` | Pizza baking | Yes - belt speed config |
159	| `CLAMSHELL` | Grilling burgers, sandwiches | Yes - top/bottom plate temps |
160	| `WATER_BATH` | Sous vide/re-thermalization | No |
161	| `FRIDGE` | Refrigerated storage | No |
162	| `PRESS` | Panini/flatbread pressing | No |
163	| `C_VAP` / `C-VAP` | Controlled vapor cooking | No - but has Max Hold Time |
164	| `HOT_BOX` | Hot holding | No |
165	| `MICROWAVE` | Reheating | No |
166	| `PITCO` | Commercial fryer | No |
167	| `RICE_COOKER` | Rice preparation | No |
168	| `STEAM_TABLE` | Steam heating | No - but has Max Hold Time |
169	| `TOASTER` | Toasting | No |
170	
171	### Global Appliance Config
172	
173	For `TURBO_OVEN`, `FRYER`, `PIZZA_CONVEYOR_OVEN`, and `CLAMSHELL`, a global appliance config is **required**:
174	
175	```
176	Turbo Oven: "100/90 475°F" (percent time/windspeed temperature)
177	Fryer: "325°F" or "350°F"
178	Pizza Conveyor: Conveyor setting
179	Clamshell: "Top: 450F, Bottom: 450F, Gap: 308mm"
180	```
181	
182	Global appliance settings are stored in [../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/mongo_batch_recipe_v2/global_appliance_settings.md](../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/mongo_batch_recipe_v2/global_appliance_settings.md) and appliance programs in [../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/mongo_batch_recipe_v2/appliance_programs.md](../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/mongo_batch_recipe_v2/appliance_programs.md).
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Parking Spots
187	
188	For COMPLETE and VEND activities, a parking spot is required:
189	
190	| Parking Spot | Description |
191	|--------------|-------------|
192	| `AMBIENT` | Room temperature holding |
193	| `WARM` | Heated holding |
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Step Structure
198	
199	Each step within a task contains:
200	
201	### Step-Level Fields
202	
203	| Field | Description | Required |
204	|-------|-------------|----------|
205	| `step_order` | Integer 1-99, determines sequence | Yes |
206	| `step` | Display step number (can match order) | Yes |
207	| `mapping_option` | Customization option this step applies to | No |
208	| `activity` | COOK, GARNISH, COMPLETE, VEND, PACKAGE | Yes |
209	| `appliance` | Equipment used (COOK activity only) | For COOK |
210	| `step_time` | Total time for step (minutes:seconds) | Yes if COOK/GARNISH |
211	| `cook_time` | Active cooking time | For COOK |
212	| `resting_time` | Resting/cooling time | No |
213	| `max_hold_time` | Maximum hold time (for COOK with certain appliances) | No |
214	| `batch_limit` | Max items per batch (>=1 for COOK) | For COOK |
215	| `step_dependency` | Comma-separated list of prerequisite steps | No |
216	| `parking_spot` | AMBIENT or WARM (for COMPLETE/VEND) | For COMPLETE/VEND |
217	
218	### Step Dependencies
219	
220	- Format: comma-separated step orders (e.g., "1, 2, 3")
221	- Dependencies must be steps with order less than current step
222	- No cyclical dependencies allowed (1→2→1 invalid)
223	- No redundant dependencies (if 2 depends on 1, and 3 depends on 2, then 3 shouldn't also list 1)
224	
225	### Sub-Step Fields
226	
227	Each step contains one or more sub-steps with:
228	
229	| Field | Description |
230	|-------|-------------|
231	| `sub_steps_order` | Order within the step |
232	| `sub_steps_title` | Instruction title (required) |
233	| `mapping_option_item` | BOM item or customization option this applies to |
234	| `text_color` | Visual highlight (Green, Beet, Orange, Grape, Violet, Juniper) |
235	| `is_cooking_eligible` | Whether this sub-step represents a cooked component |
236	| `kds_portion` | Use KDS portion conversion for display |
237	| `hot_hold_eligible_step` | Can this step use hot hold instruction |
238	
239	---
240	
241	## Hot Hold System
242	
243	Hot hold allows pre-cooking items and holding them warm, then re-thermalizing when ordered.
244	
245	### Hot Hold Eligible Step
246	
247	A step can be marked as "Hot Hold eligible" when:
248	1. Activity = COOK
249	2. Sub-step mapped to a hot hold eligible item (packaged item with HH instructions)
250	3. Or sub-step mapped to customization option whose related item is HH eligible
251	
252	### Hot Hold vs A La Minute Views
253	
254	- **A La Minute View**: Default cooking instructions (make when ordered)
255	- **Hot Hold View**: Retherm → Hold workflow for pre-cooked items
256	
257	When a step has a hot hold eligible sub-step, users can toggle between A La Minute and Hot Hold views.
258	
259	### Hot Hold Step Display
260	
261	When showing Hot Hold instructions:
262	- Activity-Appliance: `Retherm-{appliance}, Holding-{appliance}`
263	- Time: `Step time: {labor + retherm}, Retherm time: {retherm}, Hold time: {hold}`
264	- Parameters: `Cooking Phase: Hot Hold, Batch Limit: {limit}, Parking Spot`
265	
266	---
267	
268	## Apply To: Restaurants and Options
269	
270	Line builds can be scoped to specific restaurants and/or customization options.
271	
272	### Apply to Restaurants
273	
274	| Value | Behavior |
275	|-------|----------|
276	| `All` | Default line build for all restaurants |
277	| Specific HDRs | Exception line build for named restaurants |
278	
279	### Apply to Option/Option Value
280	
281	When "Multi versions vs options" toggle is enabled:
282	- Create different line builds per customization selection
283	- Example: Different line build for "White Rice" vs "Brown Rice" choice
284	
285	### Combinations
286	
287	Line builds can combine restaurant and option scoping:
288	- Line Build 1: Restaurant A, Choose Rice = White Rice
289	- Line Build 2: Restaurant A, Choose Rice = Brown Rice
290	- Line Build 3: Restaurant B, Choose Rice = White Rice
291	
292	---
293	
294	## Customization Mapping
295	
296	Steps and sub-steps can map to customization options:
297	
298	| Option Type | Mapping Format |
299	|-------------|----------------|
300	| Mandatory Choice | `Option Name - Option Value` |
301	| Optional Addition | `Option Name - Option Value` |
302	| Dish Preference | `Option Name - Option Value` |
303	| Extra Request | `Option Name - Option Value` |
304	| On the Side | `Option Value on the side` / `Option Value NOT on the side` |
305	| Optional Subtraction | `Keep {item}` / `No {item}` |
306	
307	**Note:** "Normal" and "Keep" customization options are removed from step-level mapping. Use BOM line items instead. See [customization.md](customization.md) for option types.
308	
309	---
310	
311	## Query Patterns
312	
313	### Get Line Build for a Menu Item
314	
315	```sql
316	SELECT
317	  ilb.item_number,
318	  ei.name as item_name,
319	  ilb.procedures_step_order,
320	  ilb.procedures_cooking_phase,
321	  ilb.procedures_appliance,
322	  ilb.procedures_activity,
323	  ilb.cooking_time,
324	  ilb.hold_time
325	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_line_builds` ilb
326	LEFT JOIN `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.effective_items` ei
327	  ON ilb.item_number = CAST(ei.item_number AS STRING)
328	  AND ei.deleted = false
329	WHERE ilb.item_number = '8009068'
330	  AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() BETWEEN TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_start_time) AND TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_end_time)
331	ORDER BY ilb.procedures_step_order;
332	```
333	
334	### Find Items by Appliance
335	
336	```sql
337	SELECT DISTINCT
338	  ilb.item_number,
339	  ei.name as item_name,
340	  ilb.procedures_appliance,
341	  ilb.cooking_time
342	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_line_builds` ilb
343	LEFT JOIN `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.effective_items` ei
344	  ON ilb.item_number = CAST(ei.item_number AS STRING)
345	  AND ei.deleted = false
346	WHERE ilb.procedures_appliance = 'FRYER'
347	  AND ei.object_type = 'MENU'
348	  AND ei.item_status = 'ACTIVE'
349	  AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() BETWEEN TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_start_time) AND TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_end_time)
350	ORDER BY ei.name;
351	```
352	
353	### Analyze Cooking Phase Distribution
354	
355	```sql
356	SELECT
357	  ilb.procedures_cooking_phase,
358	  COUNT(DISTINCT ilb.item_number) as item_count
359	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_line_builds` ilb
360	WHERE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() BETWEEN TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_start_time) AND TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_end_time)
361	  AND ilb.procedures_cooking_phase IS NOT NULL
362	GROUP BY ilb.procedures_cooking_phase
363	ORDER BY item_count DESC;
364	```
365	
366	### Find Hot-Hold Eligible Items
367	
368	```sql
369	SELECT DISTINCT
370	  ilb.item_number,
371	  ei.name as item_name,
372	  ilb.hold_time
373	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_line_builds` ilb

378	  AND ei.object_type = 'MENU'

380	  AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() BETWEEN TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_start_time) AND TIMESTAMP(ilb.service_end_time)
381	ORDER BY ei.name;

839	## Validation Rules
840	
841	Line builds have extensive validation at multiple levels.
842	
843	### Line Build Level Validations
844	
845	| Rule | Error Message |
846	|------|---------------|
847	| Duplicate task mapping | "Unable to save. Cannot map the same option to multiple tasks." |
848	| Missing Apply to Option value | "Please set apply to option/option values" |
849	| Duplicate line build exists | "This Line Build has already existed" |
850	
851	### Task Level Validations
852	
853	| Rule | Error Message |
854	|------|---------------|
855	| Task mapping conflicts with line build | "The following task is conflict with the line build: task {name}" |
856	| Task step conflicts with task option | "The following sub-step/step is conflict with the task: step # in task {name}" |
857	| Duplicate VEND mapping in task | Cannot map same BOM item/option to multiple VEND steps in same task |
858	
859	### Step Level Validations
860	
861	**Complete Step Rules:**
862	| Rule | Error Message |
863	|------|---------------|
864	| No complete step | "Must have at least one Complete step: task {name}" |
865	| Complete not last step | "The complete step must be the last step except Bag Steps: {task name}" |
866	| Duplicate complete step order | "Complete step order must be unique: task {name}" |
867	| Same option value on multiple completes | "Duplicated complete step" |
868	
869	**Step Order Rules:**
870	| Rule | Error Message |
871	|------|---------------|
872	| Duplicate step order (different options) | "Duplicate step order: step #, step # in {task name}" |
873	| Cyclical dependency | "Step dependency should be in format of '1, 2, 3'" |
874	| Dependency on later step | Step order must be greater than all dependencies |
875	
876	**Activity-Specific Rules:**
877	| Activity | Validation |
878	|----------|------------|
879	| COOK | Appliance required; step time > cook time; cook time > 0; batch limit >= 1 |
880	| GARNISH | Step time > 0; cook time = 0; resting time = 0 |
881	| COMPLETE | Parking spot required; must have sub-step with title |
882	| VEND | Mapping item required; parking spot required |
883	
884	### Sub-Step Level Validations
885	
886	| Rule | Error Message |
887	|------|---------------|
888	| Option conflicts with step | "Option value(s) of sub step(s) is conflict with the Option Value of its step" |
889	| Missing mapping option when step has one | "Sub step (in step #) is missing mapping option" |
890	| KDS Portion missing conversion | "Missing KDS Portion Conversion, please uncheck it or revise it on component item {number}" |

919	## Integration with Sequencing
920	
921	Line build data informs kitchen sequencing through the **forecasted procedure times pipeline**:
922	
923	```
924	item_line_builds (cooking_time, hold_time)
925	  → dbt: hdr_ops_line_build_recommendations (ALM overrides applied)
926	  → dbt: fct_ops_line_build (aggregated per procedure + variance)
927	  → MongoDB: cooking-optimization.line_build_procedure_times (batch_swap)
928	  → KDS reads at runtime for sequencing decisions
929	```
930	
931	**Key insight**: The `cooking_time` configured in CookBook is the default, but `fct_ops_line_build` may override it with Actual Line Median (ALM) data when sufficient observations exist at the HDR, mature network, or full network level. The `forecasted_time_variance_seconds` field captures the stddev of actuals.
932	
933	**Refresh**: `brd-refresh-bq` DAG (every 3 hours); rolling window of 3 days back + 1 day forward.

18	
19	# Cookbook Line Build
20	
21	A line build is the **kitchen execution blueprint** for a menu item. It tells the Kitchen Display System (KDS) what to do: which station, what equipment, how long, and in what sequence.
22	
23	## Four-Level Hierarchy
24	
25	| Level | Name | Business Meaning |
26	|-------|------|-----------------|
27	| 1 | **LineBuild** | Complete operational flow for one item (or option scope) |
28	| 2 | **Task** | Named parallel workflow (one per cooking path) |
29	| 3 | **Step (Procedure)** | Single kitchen action: one activity type, one appliance, one set of timing |
30	| 4 | **Sub-step (ProcedureStep)** | Specific instruction mapped to one BOM ingredient or customization option |
31	
32	An item can have **multiple line builds**, each scoped by **restaurant** and/or **customization option value**.
33	
34	## Activity Types and KDS Stations
35	
36	| Activity | KDS Station | What it does |
37	|----------|------------|-------------|
38	| **COOK** | Hot Pod | Active cooking (turbo oven, fryer, etc.). Requires appliance + cook time > 0. |
39	| **GARNISH** | Cold Pod | Cold assembly, pressing, toasting. No appliance. Cook time = 0. |
40	| **COMPLETE** | Expo | Final check, packaging, handoff. Must be last non-Vend step. |
41	| **VEND** | Vending pod | Dispense pre-packaged component. |
42	| **IK Step** | Intelligent Kitchen | Route IK-eligible components to the IK machine. |
43	
44	## Key Configuration Rules
45	
46	**COOK**: Appliance required. Cook time > 0. Batch limit required. Four appliances need Global Appliance Config: Turbo Oven, Fryer Basket, Pizza Conveyor Oven, Clamshell Griddle.
47	
48	**COMPLETE**: At least one required. Must be last (Vend after is OK). Requires Parking Spot (AMBIENT or WARM).
49

19	
20	# Cookbook 40-41 Model
21	
22	The 40/41 model separates **what gets consumed** at IKC locations from **what gets ordered** from the warehouse. This distinction is critical for inventory analysis — confusing the two leads to incorrect procurement and stock-level analysis.
23	
24	## The Two Item Types
25	
26	| Type | Prefix | Role | Appears in Purchase Orders |
27	|------|--------|------|---------------------------|
28	| **HDR Consumable** | 40* | What's consumed at HDR/IKC | ❌ No |
29	| **WSKU** | 41* | What's ordered from warehouse | ✅ Yes |
30	
31	Each 40\* item is linked 1:1 to at least one 41\* WSKU via the `hdr_consumable_item_number` field on the 41\* item. One 40\* can have multiple 41\* WSKUs (different pack sizes), but only ONE is "active for ordering."
32	
33	## Analysis Rules
34	
35	| Analysis Type | Use |
36	|---------------|-----|
37	| Consumption at kitchen level | 40\* items |
38	| Procurement and ordering | 41\* items |
39	| Link them | `41*.hdr_consumable_item_number = 40*.item_number` |
40	
41	## The Pack Relationship Chain
42	
43	The 40/41 model connects to packaged items (88\*) through a supply chain:
44	
45	```
46	88* PACKAGED ← fulfillment option ← 41* WSKU ← linked ← 40* HDR CONSUMABLE
47	```
48	
49	When dormanting an 88\* item, the 5-step decision tree (MD-17876) must consider whether it's the sole fulfillment option for a 41\* that feeds an active 40\* consumable in live menus. Dormanting the wrong 88\* silently breaks the kitchen supply chain.
50	
51	## Key States and Actions
52	
53	### Activate for Ordering
54	A 41\* WSKU must have "Active for Ordering" toggled before the paired 40\* can be ordered. Both items must be published.
55	
56	### Hot Holding
57	40\* items carry hot holding instructions: retherm appliance/time, holding appliance/time, batch limits. These feed into IKC station operations.
58	
59	### Dormant Rules
60	- **40\*/41\* excluded from automated weekly bulk dormant job** — must be dormanted manually
61	- 41\* cannot be dormanted while `active_for_ordering = true` AND linked 40\* not yet dormant
62	- Dormanting 41\* triggers nutrition recalculation of linked 40\*
63	- Post-cutover: 41\* items no longer dormanted separately — managed through the 40\* item
64	
65	### Sold Status
66	WSKU (41\*) has no direct service date source. Its Sold Status inherits from the linked 40\* HDR Consumable.
67	
68	
69	## Common Pitfall
70	
71	**Using 40\* for procurement analysis**: 40\* items don't appear in purchase orders or inventory receipts. Always use 41\* items for ordering/procurement queries, and link back to 40\* for consumption context.

8	---
9	
10	# HDR Consumables - The 40 Model
11	
12	HDR Consumable Items (40* prefix) and WSKUs (41* prefix) together form the "40 Model" - Wonder's system for tracking consumable inventory at HDRs (High Density Restaurants). This model separates the **consumable representation** (40*) from the **stockable/orderable representation** (41*).
13	
14	> **Confluence Source**: "HDR Consumable Item 40 Detail" (MD-15424) and "WSKUs & Consumables Grid" pages in Cookbook product documentation.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Essential Filter (ALWAYS USE)
19	
20	When querying HDR consumable items:
21	
22	```sql
23	WHERE effective = true
24	  AND deleted = false
25	  AND item_status != 'DORMANT'
26	```
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Overview
31	
32	The 40 Model establishes a clean separation between:
33	
34	1. **HDR Consumable Items (40*)**: What gets consumed/tracked at HDRs - the consumable representation
35	2. **WSKUs (41*)**: What gets ordered/stocked from the warehouse - the stockable representation
36	
37	**Key Relationship**: A single 40* item can have multiple 41* WSKUs linked to it (different pack sizes), but only **one 41* is "active for ordering"** at any given time.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Item Number Prefixes
42	
43	| Prefix | Object Type | Description | Example |
44	|--------|-------------|-------------|---------|
45	| `40*` | HDR_CONSUMABLE_ITEM | Items consumed/tracked at HDR level | 4000031, 4000053 |
46	| `41*` | WSKU | Wonder SKU - orderable warehouse items | 410001 |
47	| `88*` | PACKAGED | Pre-packaged items (legacy, being replaced by 40/41) | 8800311 |
48	| `5**/80*/88*` | Various | Legacy consumable items migrated to 40* | Various |
49	
50	**Naming Convention**:
51	- 40* items: `{Original Name} HDR` - e.g., "Pulled Pork [Pouch, 150g] 3.0 HDR"
52	- 41* items: `{Name} WSKU` - e.g., "Pulled Pork [Pouch, 150g] 3.0 WSKU"
53	
54	See [item-master.md](item-master.md) for the full item number prefix taxonomy and object types.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## The 40 Model Explained
59	
60	### Stockable vs Consumable
61	
62	The 40 Model separates two concerns:
63	
64	| Aspect | 40* (HDR Consumable) | 41* (WSKU) |
65	|--------|---------------------|------------|
66	| Purpose | Track consumption at HDR | Track inventory ordering |
67	| Used By | Pantry, BOM, Kitchen | Supply Chain, Ordering |
68	| Quantity | Consumption quantity | Pack size quantity |
69	| Relationship | Has linked WSKUs | Links to one 40* item |
70	
71	### Why This Matters
72	
73	**Example**: A 40* item "Pulled Pork HDR" might have two 41* WSKUs:
74	- `410001`: 150g pouch (active for ordering)
75	- `410002`: 300g pouch (inactive, legacy size)
76	
77	Both WSKUs link to the same consumable item, allowing:
78	- Pantry to see total on-hand inventory across both pack sizes
79	- Ordering to route through the currently active WSKU only
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Active for Ordering
84	
85	Each 40* item must have exactly one 41* WSKU marked as **"Active for Ordering"**.
86	
87	**Rules**:
88	1. Only one 41* per 40* can be active at a time
89	2. Activating a new 41* automatically deactivates the previous one
90	3. Cannot deactivate the last active 41* for a non-dormant 40*
91	4. Both active and inactive 41* items are synced to downstream systems (Pantry, Ladle)
92	
93	**Downstream Behavior**:
94	- **Pantry**: Sees all linked 41* items (tracks on-hand inventory for both)
95	- **Ladle**: Uses only the "active for ordering" 41* for new orders
96	
97	---
98	
99	## Data Storage
100	
101	### HDR Consumable Items (40*)
102	
103	Stored in [`item_versions`](../tables/secure-recipe-prod/recipe_v2/item_versions.md) with `object_type = 'HDR_CONSUMABLE_ITEM'`:
104	
105	| Field | Description |
106	|-------|-------------|
107	| `item_number` | 40* identifier |
108	| `name` | Item name with "HDR" suffix |
109	| `object_type` | 'HDR_CONSUMABLE_ITEM' |
110	| `production_start_time` | When item starts production |
111	| `service_start_time` | When item starts service |
112	| `sold_status` | Current sale status |
113	| `bom_unit` | Unit of measure for BOM |
114	| `inventory_unit` | Unit for inventory tracking |
115	
116	**40* Item Characteristics**:
117	- Only has 1 version (no version history)
118	- Cannot create variants
119	- Not synced to ERP
120	- Shows "Pack Size List" card with linked WSKUs
121	
122	### WSKUs (41*)
123	
124	Stored in [`item_versions`](../tables/secure-recipe-prod/recipe_v2/item_versions.md) with `object_type = 'WSKU'`:
125	
126	| Field | Description |
127	|-------|-------------|
128	| `item_number` | 41* identifier |
129	| `name` | Item name with "WSKU" suffix |
130	| `object_type` | 'WSKU' |
131	| `consumable_item_number` | Linked 40* item |
132	| `consumable_quantity` | Quantity of 40* per WSKU unit |
133	| `active_for_ordering` | Boolean - is this the active WSKU? |
134	
135	**41* Item Characteristics**:
136	- Cannot create new versions
137	- Cannot create variants
138	- Not synced to ERP
139	- Shows Hot Hold, Fulfillment Option, SKU Unit Size Mapping cards
140	
141	> The open mirror of `item_versions` is available under [../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/recipe_v2/item_versions.md](../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/recipe_v2/item_versions.md).
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Usages Card (40* Items)
146	
147	HDR Consumable items have a "Usages" card with four tabs:
148	
149	| Tab | Description |
150	|-----|-------------|
151	| Component Usages | Where this 40* appears as a BOM component |
152	| BOM Usages | Where this 40* appears in BOMs |
153	| Customization Usages | Where this 40* is a customization option |
154	| Linked WSKUs | All 41* items linked to this 40* |
155	
156	---
157	
158	## Data Migration Context
159	
160	The 40 Model was created by migrating existing consumable items (5*/80*/88*) to the new structure:
161	
162	**Migration Rules**:
163	1. Create new 40* item from existing consumable
164	2. If 41* WSKU was both stockable AND consumable with qty != 1ea, create separate 40*
165	3. Replace legacy consumable linkages (5*/80*/88*) with new 40* in WSKU definitions
166	4. If consumable qty = 1ea and item equals itself, no new 40* needed
167	5. Record linkage between new 40* and source 5*/80*/88* item
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Query Patterns
172	
173	### List All Active HDR Consumable Items (40*)
174	
175	```sql
176	SELECT
177	  item_number,
178	  name,
179	  item_status,
180	  sold_status
181	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.effective_items`
182	WHERE item_number LIKE '40%'
183	  AND deleted = false
184	  AND item_status = 'ACTIVE'
185	ORDER BY name;
186	```
187	
188	### List All WSKUs (41*)
189	
190	```sql
191	SELECT
192	  item_number,
193	  name,
194	  item_status,
195	  sold_status
196	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.effective_items`
197	WHERE item_number LIKE '41%'
198	  AND deleted = false
199	  AND item_status = 'ACTIVE'
200	ORDER BY name;
201	```
202	
203	### Find WSKUs Linked to a 40* Item
204	
205	```sql
206	-- Find all 41* WSKUs that link to a specific 40* consumable item
207	SELECT
208	  iv.item_number as wsku_number,
209	  iv.name as wsku_name,
210	  JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.item_number') as consumable_item,
211	  JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.quantity') as consumable_qty,
212	  JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.active_for_ordering') as active_for_ordering
213	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_versions` iv
214	WHERE iv.effective = true
215	  AND iv.deleted = false
216	  AND iv.item_status != 'DORMANT'
217	  AND iv.object_type = 'WSKU'
218	  AND JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.item_number') = '4000053';
219	```
220	
221	### Find Active WSKU for a 40* Item
222	
223	```sql
224	SELECT
225	  iv.item_number as wsku_number,
226	  iv.name as wsku_name,
227	  JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.item_number') as consumable_item
228	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_versions` iv
229	WHERE iv.effective = true
230	  AND iv.deleted = false
231	  AND iv.item_status != 'DORMANT'
232	  AND iv.object_type = 'WSKU'
233	  AND JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.item_number') = '4000053'
234	  AND CAST(JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.active_for_ordering') AS BOOL) = true;
235	```
236	
237	### Find 40* Items with Multiple WSKUs
238	
239	```sql
240	WITH wsku_counts AS (
241	  SELECT
242	    JSON_VALUE(iv.consumable_item, '$.item_number') as consumable_item,
243	    COUNT(*) as wsku_count
244	  FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_versions` iv
245	  WHERE iv.effective = true
246	    AND iv.deleted = false
247	    AND iv.item_status != 'DORMANT'
248	    AND iv.object_type = 'WSKU'
249	  GROUP BY 1
250	)
251	SELECT
252	  wc.consumable_item,
253	  ei.name as consumable_name,
254	  wc.wsku_count
255	FROM wsku_counts wc
256	LEFT JOIN `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.effective_items` ei
257	  ON wc.consumable_item = ei.item_number
258	  AND ei.deleted = false
259	WHERE wc.wsku_count > 1
260	ORDER BY wc.wsku_count DESC;
261	```
262	
263	### Find Menu Items Using a 40* Consumable
264	
265	```sql
266	SELECT DISTINCT
267	  m.item_number as menu_item,
268	  m.name as menu_item_name
269	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_versions` m,
270	UNNEST(JSON_EXTRACT_ARRAY(m.bom_header, '$.bom_lines')) AS bom_line
271	WHERE m.effective = true
272	  AND m.deleted = false
273	  AND m.item_status != 'DORMANT'
274	  AND m.object_type = 'MENU'
275	  AND JSON_VALUE(bom_line, '$.item_number') LIKE '40%'
276	ORDER BY menu_item;
277	```
278	
279	### Count Items by 40/41 Type
280	
281	```sql
282	SELECT
283	  CASE
284	    WHEN item_number LIKE '40%' THEN 'HDR_CONSUMABLE (40*)'
285	    WHEN item_number LIKE '41%' THEN 'WSKU (41*)'
286	    ELSE 'OTHER'
287	  END as item_type,
288	  COUNT(*) as count
289	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.effective_items`
290	WHERE deleted = false
291	  AND item_status = 'ACTIVE'
292	  AND (item_number LIKE '40%' OR item_number LIKE '41%')
293	GROUP BY 1
294	ORDER BY 1;
295	```
296	
297	### Find Consumable Items NOT Using 40 Model
298	
299	Find items that are flagged as consumable but haven't been migrated to the 40 Model yet:
300	
301	```sql
302	SELECT
303	  iv.item_number,
304	  i.enable_40_model_date,
305	  i.enable_40_model,
306	  iv.is_consumable_inventory,
307	  iv.name
308	FROM `secure-recipe-prod.recipe_v2.item_versions` iv
309	LEFT JOIN `wonder-recipe-prod.mongo_batch_recipe_v2.items` i
310	  ON iv.item_number = i.item_number
311	WHERE iv.is_consumable_inventory = true
312	  AND iv.item_status != 'DORMANT'
313	  AND iv.deleted = false
314	  AND iv.effective = true
315	  AND iv.object_type IN ('INGREDIENT', 'PACKAGED', 'RECIPE')
316	  AND i.enable_40_model_date IS NULL;  -- Not yet migrated to 40 Model
317	```
318	
319	**Note**: `enable_40_model_date` being NULL indicates items that are consumable but haven't been converted to the new 40*/41* structure. The `items` table referenced here is [../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/mongo_batch_recipe_v2/items.md](../tables/wonder-recipe-prod/mongo_batch_recipe_v2/items.md).
320	
321	---
322	
323	## Permissions
324	
325	| Permission | Allows |
326	|------------|--------|
327	| Create WSKU | Creating new 41* items |
328	| Edit WSKU | Modifying 41* item details |
329	| Edit Pack Size | Changing consumable quantity in WSKU |
330	| N/A | Creating new 40* versions (not allowed) |
331	| N/A | Creating 40* variants (not allowed) |
332	
333	---
334	
335	## Critical Rules
336	
337	1. **Always include `deleted = false`** when querying any item data
338	2. **40* items have only 1 version** - no version history or variants allowed
339	3. **One active WSKU per 40*** - only one 41* can be "active for ordering" at a time
340	4. **Both active and inactive WSKUs sync** - downstream systems see all linked 41* items
341	5. **Pantry tracks all WSKUs** - inventory aggregates across all linked pack sizes
342	6. **Ladle uses active WSKU only** - ordering routes through the active 41*
343	7. **41* items are NOT synced to ERP** - they exist only in Cookbook/PCS
344	
345	---
